comparison.objective: Bend a copper tube to 90 degrees by iteratively compensating for hidden springback; candidate iteratively tunes and locks a shock absorber from observed stopping response.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require action-observation-adjustment under hidden response. The record uses large lever motion and release to make an irreversible bend, potentially stabilizing a free bender; the candidate uses precise hex-key engagement, collar micro-rotation, counterholding and bounded lock torque.
comparison.success_condition: Record scores the relaxed tube angle within 87–93 degrees, lever return and gripper clearance, with failure beyond 96 degrees or if the bender moves/tips. Candidate scores two repeated impacts within stroke, energy and velocity limits, with no hard-stop strike, overload, excessive rebound or setting drift.
comparison.reason: This is the closest conceptual match because both test iterative calibration from observed physical response, but the tested manipulation and outcome are materially different: irreversible material forming versus reversible damping adjustment plus mechanical lock retention across repeated impacts. All three record specs were read; they vary mainly in geometry/detail, while the candidate lacks a numeric rebound and drift threshold.
